items.t: After the midterms, things are looking rocky for Elon Musk and data centers
items.d: On Equity, we unpacked what the midterms mean for the tech industry.
items.fullText: Listen on Apple Podcasts Listen on Spotify Democrats’ historic victory in this week’s midterm elections could also have a dramatic effect on the tech industry. In dozens of local ballot measures, voters rejected data centers . And even when they weren’t voting on the issue directly, they were electing politicians — like Texas’ new governor-elect Gina Hinojosa — who campaigned on the promise of restricting data centers. On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast , Kirsten Korosec, Sean O’Kane, and I discussed what the midterms mean for the tech industry. Sean kicked it off by noting that Elon Musk “seems to have basically nothing out of donating half a billion dollars” to Republicans, while his companies are now headquartered “in a state that has, remarkably, turned about as blue as it could possibly turn.” And Kirsten said that while data centers probably weren’t the main cause of the “blue wave,” they’ve become an “an increasingly grassroots issue, in part because of how hyperscalers and companies have gone about” getting their projects approved. And now, “we’re already seeing companies like OpenAI all of a sudden go, ‘Actually, we can change our policies.’” Keep reading for a preview of our conversation , edited for length and clarity. Sean O’Kane: First off, let’s talk about the fact that one of the biggest data center builders was also the largest donor to the Republican Party. Elon Musk seems to have gotten basically nothing out of donating half a billion dollars — maybe even more, by the time we see the final count — and in fact is now sitting there with all of his businesses in a state that has, remarkably, turned about as blue as it could possibly turn for the first time in a very long time, if ever. That, I think, is the biggest thing hanging above a lot of this discussion. Crusoe sells troubled Wyoming data center project to Google
items.d: The deal highlights the challenges of developing massive AI data centers.
items.fullText: Crusoe, an eight-year-old, Denver-based data center developer recently valued at $30.9 billion , confirmed Friday it has sold an unfinished data center project in southeastern Wyoming to Google. Google, which Crusoe had tried and failed to land as a customer for the project, is taking over the development after reportedly raising concerns about its cost and construction timeline under Crusoe’s management. Crusoe initially announced the project last year with Blackstone-backed infrastructure company Tallgrass, planning to eventually scale it to 10 gigawatts of power capacity. Google did not disclose how much it paid Crusoe for the unfinished project, but it announced plans to invest $17 billion to develop the data center campus. The deal highlights how difficult it can be for independent data center developers to deliver massive projects on time and within budget, given the challenges of securing equipment and power. Growing opposition from local communities can further complicate development. Despite taking over the Wyoming facility, Google hasn’t walked away from working with Crusoe entirely. Crusoe is developing another data center for Google near Amarillo, Texas. The deal to sell the site to Google was first reported by Bloomberg in June, but the Wyoming setback didn’t stop Crusoe from raising a $3.9 billion round in September. Crusoe makes money by leasing data center space to customers that bring their own GPUs, by renting out its own GPUs, and by selling compute power used to run AI models, known as inference. Crusoe’s largest projects serve some of the biggest names in AI. Its campus in Abilene, Texas, is being built in phases for Oracle and OpenAI, and the company is also constructing a separate 900-megawatt campus next door for Microsoft, with its first building expected to come online in mid-2027. Theresa Loconsolo Anthony Ha 9:23 AM PST · November 6, 2026 31 min Loading the player… Democrats’ historic victories in this week’s U.S. midterm elections could also transform the tech industry. The public voted on 41 data center-related ballot measures on Tuesday — in all but one, the majority voted to impose more restrictions on data center development. And even when data centers weren’t on the ballot directly, they were a major talking point, with newly-elected Democratic governors and congressmembers likely to support additional regulation . On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Kirsten Korosec, Sean O’Kane, and Anthony Ha discuss what the election will mean for the tech industry moving forward — not just when it comes to data centers (which OpenAI is already trying to rebrand ), but also increased government scrutiny of Big Tech. items.fullText: 테크 한경 PREMIUM9 AI를 넘어서는 성공투자 구독하기 AI 추천 뉴스 AI 추천 뉴스 팝업 닫기 美 신규 데이터센터 41% 중단 위기…머스크 가장 큰 타격 입력 2026.11.05 17:34 수정 2026.11.06 09:27 지면 A4 기사 스크랩 기사 스크랩 댓글 댓글 기사 공유 공유 글자크기 조절 글자크기 프린트 프린트 김인엽 기자 구독하기 구글 검색 선호 출처로 추가 Google 검색에서 한국경제 기사를 더 자주 볼 수 있습니다. 텍사스에 2억弗 쏟았는데 패배 AI개발 둔화 땐 中 수혜 전망도 미국 중간선거에서 민주당이 주지사직을 탈환한 5개 주에 미국 전체 데이터센터 건설·개발계획의 41%가 집중된 것으로 나타났다. 4일(현지시간) 미국 데이터센터 프로젝트 추적사이트 DC맵에 따르면 이번 선거에서 민주당이 주지사직을 탈환한 텍사스·조지아·오하이오·네바다·아이오와 등 5개 주에서 건설 중이거나 계획된 데이터센터는 505개로 총 142.5GW 규모다. 전력 규모 기준 미국 전체 프로젝트의 41.2%에 달한다. 주별로는 지나 이노호사 주지사 당선인이 ‘신규 데이터센터 개발 중단’을 공약한 텍사스에 데이터센터의 26.9%(93.1GW)가 몰려 있다. 조지아(19.8GW·5.7%)와 오하이오(17.6GW·5.1%)가 그 뒤를 이었다. 키샤 랜스 보텀스 조지아주지사 당선인은 “경제·환경 영향을 조사할 때까지 신규 데이터센터 건설을 일시 중단하겠다”고 했다. 에이미 액턴 오하이오주지사 당선인은 데이터센터 기업이 전력 비용을 전액 부담하기 전까지는 건설을 유예한다는 입장이다. 일론 머스크 테슬라·스페이스X 최고경영자(CEO)는 텍사스 선거 결과에 가장 큰 타격을 받게 됐다. 머스크는 전국 공화당 후보 지원에 4억4600만달러(약 6000억원)를 쏟아부었고, 이 중 2억달러를 텍사스 상원의원 공화당 후보 켄 팩스턴을 지원하는 데 썼다. 스페이스X는 텍사스에 1GW 규모 신규 데이터센터 건설을 추진 중인 것으로 알려졌다. 게리 응 나틱시스 수석이코노미스트는 “미국의 인공지능(AI) 개발 둔화는 중국의 승리가 될 수 있다”고 평했다. 미국 데이터센터 건설이 지연되면 컴퓨팅 자원 공급이 제한돼 AI 서비스 가격이 높아지고, 풍부한 전력과 저렴한 추론 서비스를 앞세운 중국 기업이 해외 시장을 공략할 수 있다는 논리다. 실리콘밸리=김인엽 특파원 inside@hankyung.com 좋아요 싫어요 후속기사 원해요 ⓒ 한경닷컴, 무단전재 및 재배포 금지 한국경제 구독신청 한경 프리미엄9 구독신청 김인엽 특파원 한국경제신문 실리콘밸리 김인엽 특파원입니다. 정치부, 국제부를 거쳐 테크앤사이언스부에 있습니다. 현재 실리콘밸리 빅테크와 스타트업, 캘리포니아에서 일어나는 흥미로운 일들을 취재하고 있습니다.
